vibe.rationale: Vibe 3 — a decisive downgrade from the July 13 evening's Vibe 5 ('No Fourth Exchange') driven by two overnight structural developments that together constitute the most significant single-session geopolitical deterioration since the July 7 US strike resumption. First and most consequential: the fourth US-Iran kinetic exchange is confirmed. The US struck Iran for the third consecutive day (July 12/13/14 cycle), and Iran retaliated with tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz — at least two UAE-flagged tankers struck, 1 Indian crew member killed, 8 wounded. This is the first confirmed Hormuz tanker casualty of the 2026 conflict arc. The WTI response ($80.55, +3% Tuesday open; Brent $86.85, +4.3%) is the largest single-session oil price move since the February 28 crisis opening, and represents a full reversal of the July 11 normalization signal that brought WTI to the $71-72 range. Second: Trump's announcement of a plan to impose 20% shipping fees in the Strait of Hormuz materially escalates the economic conflict dimension. Citi explicitly warned this proposal raises the risk of further military escalation. The proposal — if operationalized — would transform Hormuz from a contested military transit zone into a US-taxed commercial chokepoint, a move with no precedent in maritime law and a near-guaranteed Iranian counter-escalation trigger. The MOU's three termination-instrument absences continue to hold: no SNSC formal void declaration, no CENTCOM blockade reinstatement, no Kharg Island strike. The MOU is legally operative but under the most severe stress of the 26-day arc. The Qatar diplomatic channel — the primary MOU communication architecture — has received no confirmed operational output following Iran's targeting of Doha with ballistic missiles Saturday night and two subsequent days of US-Iran exchange. The channel's silence is the single highest-priority analytical gap of the morning. June CPI T-0 releases today at 8:30 AM ET (Cleveland nowcast 3.8% YoY). The timing irony is acute: any June disinflation signal — including a headline flip to negative on energy base effects — reflects June oil prices ($65-74 WTI), not the current $80.55 reality. The forward CPI trajectory is moving in the wrong direction in real time even as the backward-looking data may print positively. Warsh's September FOMC deflationary thesis is under maximum constraint: three required favorable conditions (Hormuz normalization below $72, Russian refining recovery, commodity relief) are all deteriorating simultaneously. Upgrade to Vibe 4 requires: diplomatic channel confirmation of active Oman or Qatar-Pakistan mediation output; WTI retreating below $77 during Tuesday session; Iranian tanker attacks characterized as one-time retaliation rather than sustained campaign posture; B and O Fire continuing containment growth through Day 5 without re-escalation; June CPI confirming at or below 3.8% with core deceleration. Drop to Vibe 2 requires: MOU formally voided (SNSC declaration); CENTCOM naval blockade reinstated; additional Hormuz tanker sinkings with mass crew casualties; WTI sustained above $87 (Brent $92+); or US-Iran exchange escalating beyond aerial strike package to ground engagement or nuclear facility targeting.

items.summary: The July 14 morning brief opens on Hormuz MOU Acute Stress Day 7 with the most consequential overnight escalation since the July 7 US strike resumption. The fourth US-Iran kinetic exchange is confirmed: the United States struck Iran for the third consecutive day in the July 12-13-14 cycle, and Iran responded with tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz — at least two UAE-flagged tankers struck, with one Indian crew member confirmed killed and eight wounded. This is the first confirmed Hormuz tanker casualty of the 2026 conflict arc, and it materially shifts the analytical framing from 'contested Hormuz closure declaration' to 'active tanker warfare in the Strait.' WTI surged to $80.55 (+3% Tuesday open; Brent $86.85, +4.3%) — the highest since the February 28 crisis opening and a full reversal of the $71-72 normalization signal from July 11. The WTI move above $80 represents a new structural price level that formally forecloses the Warsh September FOMC deflationary thesis absent an immediate and dramatic de-escalation. Three MOU termination-instrument absences continue to hold: no SNSC formal void declaration, no CENTCOM naval blockade reinstatement, no Kharg Island strike. The MOU is legally operative on Day 26 but under conditions of maximum acute stress: the exchange cycle has now confirmed four separate US-Iran kinetic events since July 7, with Iran expanding its attack modalities to include tanker warfare in the waterway the MOU was designed to reopen. A critical new escalatory element: President Trump announced plans to impose a 20% shipping fee on all cargo transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Citi warned that this proposal materially raises the risk of further military escalation. The proposal has no precedent in international maritime law and, if operationalized, would transform Hormuz from a contested military transit zone into a US-taxed commercial chokepoint — a near-certain trigger for Iranian counter-escalation beyond the current tanker-attack posture. Iran also fired ballistic missiles and drones targeting Bahrain and Jordan overnight in the exchange cycle, extending the Gulf-wide attack posture first demonstrated with the Saturday night five-nation attack. The Qatar diplomatic channel remains the morning's highest-priority analytical gap. The channel was last confirmed operative on July 11 daytime; Qatar was targeted with Iranian ballistic missiles Saturday night; the subsequent fourth exchange cycle (July 12-13-14) has produced no confirmed channel output. Whether the Doha mediation architecture survived two consecutive days of US-Iran exchange — with Qatar as an Iranian missile target — is analytically unresolved. Pakistan, a secondary channel interlocutor, has not issued public statements confirming continued mediation activity. Mojtaba Khamenei (Supreme Leader since March 8, in hiding Day 131+) continues communicating only via written statements. Every Iranian negotiating signal carries the structural ambiguity of a principal-level communications architecture operating through couriers without face-to-face or voice authentication. June CPI T-0 releases today at 8:30 AM ET. Cleveland Fed nowcast: approximately 3.8% year-over-year, down from 4.2% in May. The backward-looking June data — covering a period when WTI was in the $65-74 range — may produce a headline disinflation signal (including a possible negative monthly print on energy base effects) that is analytically misleading given the current $80.55 WTI reality. The July CPI — releasing in mid-August — will capture the current energy price surge. Sixty-day nuclear technical window Day 26 (41.7% elapsed; window closes approximately August 17).

items.summary: The July 14 morning economic session opens with WTI at $80.55 — a +3% Tuesday open and a new structural benchmark that represents a complete regime shift from the $65-74 WTI range that defined the June data set. The $80.55 print is the highest oil price since the February 28 crisis opening. Brent at $86.85 (+4.3%) confirms the move is a global pricing signal rather than US-specific. Three compounding factors drive the Tuesday surge: (1) Iran's confirmed tanker attack on two UAE-flagged vessels transiting Hormuz (1 Indian crew member killed, 8 wounded) — the first Hormuz tanker casualty of the 2026 arc, establishing a live maritime-warfare risk premium on top of the existing war-risk premium; (2) the fourth US-Iran kinetic exchange confirming that no diplomatic pause has taken hold despite the MOU remaining legally operative; (3) President Trump's announcement of a plan to impose a 20% shipping fee on all Hormuz cargo — a proposal that Citi explicitly characterized as materially raising the risk of further military escalation. The Trump shipping fee, if operationalized, would represent an unprecedented assertion of US commercial authority over an international maritime strait that Iran claims as its sovereign territory. The combined effect: tanker operators face not only military risk from Iranian attacks but potential US tariff liability for transit, creating a compounding disincentive structure that reinforces the effective closure of Hormuz for commercial routing purposes regardless of CENTCOM's operational counter-declaration. June CPI T-0 releases today at 8:30 AM ET — the most consequential single economic data point of the brief's arc since May CPI on June 10. Cleveland Fed nowcast: 3.8% year-over-year (down from 4.2% in May). Kiplinger's pre-release analysis identified a possible negative monthly headline print on energy base effects from June's oil price declines (WTI was $65-74 during June). The analytical challenge: a headline June CPI confirming at 3.8% or below — or even going negative on the month — is data from a different energy price reality. At WTI $80.55 on the morning the data releases, the forward-looking inflationary signal from the Hormuz crisis has already diverged decisively from the backward-looking June data. Warsh's September FOMC deflationary thesis required three concurrent favorable conditions: (1) Hormuz WTI normalization below $72 — FORECLOSED AT $80.55; (2) Russian refinery crisis resolution — MULTI-MONTH, NOT IN PROGRESS; (3) commodity relief from tariff moderation — NOT IN PROGRESS. All three are moving in the wrong direction simultaneously on the morning the June CPI lands. CME FedWatch September hike probability — previously at 61% — is expected to see downward pressure from any positive June CPI print, but the structural energy shock means the FOMC's late-August Jackson Hole positioning will need to account for the July energy price reality, not June's. Tariff calendar: Section 122 expires July 24 (T-10); USTR Section 301 completion deadline July 20 (T-6). The 3-4 day July 20-24 gap between Section 301 completion and Section 122 expiry remains the operative importer planning concern. No White House Section 301 successor structure announced. Pharma 232 July 31 (T-17). FERC AI 30-day report July 18 (T-4 — final four days; PNW Climate Week Day 2).

items.summary: The July 14 morning infrastructure session advances through the B and O Fire Day 5 suppression arc with the prior overnight's 19% containment breakthrough as the carry-forward baseline. The B and O Fire (near Okanogan, Okanogan County WA, ignition July 9, human-caused/under investigation) achieved 19% containment overnight July 12-13 — the suppression milestone that reversed the 0%/Level 3 characterization from the July 12 morning brief. Level 2 evacuations have held in Okanogan County areas. Acreage at/near 2,900+ acres with the morning ICS-209 update pending at time of brief generation. The fire is in the east Cascades onset region on Day 17 — a period characterized by persistent east wind and low relative humidity that remain the primary suppression challenge. Additional Red Flag events are possible through the onset period.
